_: Where this fork hooks into upstream-owned files. fork/sync.mjs checks these after every replay: a merge can be textually clean and still lose a hook (upstream moved or rewrote the code around it). `min` is how many times the literal text must appear. When a port moves a hook, update the entry.

electron/main.ts.why: the gate holds every backend start and dial: runHermesStart, runPoolBackendStart and connectRegistryBackend (SSH / remote connections)
every outbound request of Electron's network stack is held until the tunnel is up
sessions created later (link titles, webviews) get the egress gate too
the update check (git / Python / feed fetches the egress gate can not see) waits for the tunnel; it lives in checkUpdates()
the tunnel is brought up as early as possible
the monitor is stopped on quit
at startup, an old fork bundle on a newer official runtime hands over to fork/update.mjs and boots nothing (electron/fork-update.ts)
a failed or postponed fork update is told to the user once
a build outside a fork checkout (an installer given to someone) has no 'Update now': the official update would leave it stale; it answers 'external'
the self-update shell is wired to the real app, git, the update marker and the VPN
the VPN IPC surface the renderer talks to
own AppUserModelID: own taskbar button and icon next to the official Hermes
a fork that renamed itself (Hermoso) is called by the name baked into the identity (fork/identity.json): the window title, the notices, the app menu
the AppUserModelID: the fork's own app id when its identity carries one, 'com.nousresearch.hermes.mullvad' for the Mullvad fork
the self-update notices speak in the fork's own name
every window is titled with the app's own name (Hermoso), not a literal 'Hermes'
Hermoso (Teleport, the agent bridge, the plugin installer) is created once, next to the VPN controller it works with (electron/hermoso/)
a Teleport trip left open by a crash is brought home BEFORE the VPN gate connects the tunnel, or the gate would connect in the foreign country
the bridge is up and the plugin is installed in the Hermes home before each backend starts (runHermesStart, runPoolBackendStart)
the backend gets the bridge address and token, so the agent's plugin can reach the app
the one IPC channel every Hermoso feature uses
a machine that is away on a Teleport trip is brought home before the app quits
the bridge is closed with the app

electron/preload.ts.why: the renderer bridge for the VPN IPC surface
the renderer's door to Hermoso (events pushed by main)

src/app/gateway/hooks/use-gateway-boot.t.why: the renderer's boot waits for main's gate instead of racing it
the renderer's boot budget renews while a first-run install is in progress, so a healthy install is not shown as "Hermes couldn't start" after 3 minutes (src/lib/with-timeout.ts)

src/app/contrib/wiring.tsx.why: the boot card that explains what the gate is waiting for

product-identity.cjs.why: upstream's one source of names carries the fork's names when a fork build selects its identity (HERMES_FORK_IDENTITY); a no-op otherwise

vite.config.ts.why: the wordmark a renamed fork writes across an empty chat comes from its identity, at build time
the page title (which becomes the window title once the page loads) carries the fork's name

src/components/chat/intro.tsx.why: the intro wordmark: the fork's own name when the build defines it, 'HERMES AGENT' otherwise

src/global.d.ts.why: the typed surface of window.hermesDesktop.hermoso, used by the bundled Hermoso plugin (src/plugins/hermoso/)

src/plugins/hermoso/plugin.tsx.why: the Hermoso window plugin: a bundled plugin the app discovers by itself (nothing upstream registers it); if upstream moves the plugin door this is what to port
